clock_sensitivity_conclusion: At the predeclared 5000-ms freshness sensitivity, Product keynote class medians have opposite signs on receive and exchange clocks. Their direction is therefore sensitive to the clock definition; these estimates do not establish a stable clock-independent event-class finding. The primary 250-ms controlled comparisons remain unsupported.
interpretation: Descriptive matched-control excess changes by event, reporting bundle and year; no causal effect, confidence interval or p-value.
limitations: Reference days are randomly drawn exposure controls, not certified news-free or randomized corporate announcements.
The event calendar is sourced but is not a complete blackout list of all Apple announcements or macroeconomic releases.
A scheduled keynote/call or publisher-declared release timestamp is not the exact nanosecond news reached every market participant.
Earnings-call prewindows may already contain the earnings release; overlapping anchors share one bundle and do not add independent events.
Afterhours activity and liquidity differ from regular hours. Same-clock controls do not identify a causal event-class effect.
Conditional matched latencies require accompanying match rates, full follow-up and explicit missing-support counts.
Quote-age policies affect observed cohorts, especially in quiet afterhours controls; sensitivity results do not replace an unsupported primary estimate.
Receive-clock delays include feed transport; exchange clocks need not be perfectly synchronized. Counting price matches is not causal information share.
The 2026 WWDC case informed this extension and is labelled discovery rather than counted as independent historical confirmation.
Each event anchor requires every one of its five frozen matched-control changes; missing support is not replaced or silently dropped.
Corporate-event bundles and calendar years, rather than quotes, define dependence and sample size.
Discovery events are kept separate from the historical primary summaries.
Class summaries with incomplete support describe supported bundles only, with planned and excluded counts retained.
A paired-year class comparison requires every planned bundle in both class/year strata; incomplete years remain explicitly excluded.
Cross-session event classes remain confounded with trading hours even after same-clock matched controls.
Scheduled call/keynote starts and filing acceptance times need not identify first public information.
Different clocks, freshness thresholds and horizons can define different observable event populations.
Leave-one-year-out ranges are sensitivity summaries, not confidence intervals; no p-values or causal effects are reported.
